This PR applies Mixed (FlyDSL + Gluon) MoE strategy, with a configurable threshold setting.

## Motivation

On gfx1250, there are **3 apparent lowering paths of W4A8 MoE kernels**: triton, Gluon, FlyDSL.  Profiling them reveals interesting results as below.  Experiment details: Per-layer MoE time, gpt-oss-120b, TP1, layer 18's real weights, the full MoE forward SGLang calls (routing, quant, both GEMMs), inside a CUDA graph, weights streamed from HBM; µs per layer, median of 3 passes.

| tokens | Triton (existing) | Gluon | FlyDSL | fastest | Gluon / FlyDSL |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 36 | **36** | 77 | Gluon (= Triton) | 0.47 |
| 16 | 222 | **125** | 224 | Gluon | 0.56 |
| 64 | 351 | **229** | 324 | Gluon | 0.71 |
| 128 | 403 | **276** | 345 | Gluon | 0.80 |
| 256 | 599 | **335** | 371 | Gluon | 0.90 |
| 384 | 750 | 394 | 399 | tie | 0.99 |
| 512 | 926 | 462 | **436** | FlyDSL | 1.06 |
| 1024 | 1272 | 608 | **555** | FlyDSL | 1.10 |
| 2048 | 1560 | 1015 | **758** | FlyDSL | 1.34 |
| 3072 | 2150 | 1738 | **1024** | FlyDSL | 1.70 |

- **Gluon** wins below ~320 tokens: 1.4-2.3x faster than FlyDSL below 128.
- **FlyDSL** wins from 1024 tokens on, by 1.7x at a full 3072-token prefill chunk; from 320 to 768 the two are within 6%.
- **Triton** matches Gluon only at a single token; from 4 tokens on it is 1.5-2.3x slower than the faster of the two.
- TP2 (per rank, intermediate 1440): the same picture (Gluon/FlyDSL 0.46 at 1, 0.62 at 128, 1.61 at 3072; within 7% from 320 to 1024). With uniform routing the crossover moves up to ~1024, with all tokens on 4 experts down to ~192.

FlyDSL also costs ~1 ms of CPU per eager call (Gluon and Triton ~0.3 ms), so this pays off with prefill CUDA graphs (`--cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable`), where that cost is not paid per step.

## Modifications

- `SGLANG_GFX1250_W4A8_FLYDSL=1` (default off: without it nothing changes). At load, `prepare_w4a8_gfx1250_flydsl_weights` puts the experts into FlyDSL's layout: gate/up interleaved, dims zero-padded to 256 (2880 -> 3072; the TP2 intermediate 1440 -> 1536), `moe_shuffle_weight` / `moe_shuffle_scale`, padded scales = e8m0 1.0. These buffers become the layer's parameters.
- Batches of at least `SGLANG_GFX1250_W4A8_FLYDSL_MIN_TOKENS` tokens run `aiter.fused_moe` (FlyDSL a8w4, `gate_mode=INTERLEAVE`, `quant_type=per_1x32`, `quant_dtype_a=fp8`, Swiglu with `swiglu_limit`, bias1/bias2, bf16 router weights).
- Smaller batches run `moe_gemm_a8w4` with `backend="gluon"`, `preshuffled=True`, `swizzle_mx_scale="GFX1250_SCALE"` over `moe_weight_decode_view` of the same storage (zero-copy views).
- The Gluon views are cut to dims rounded up to 128 (2880 -> 2944, activations zero-padded). With `GFX1250_SCALE` the scale descriptor ends at `K // 32` groups while the n32k4 layout stores K in 128-element chunks, so at K = 2880 the last chunk's scales would read as 0. Aligned, the Gluon path is bitwise equal to the Triton path.
- `SGLANG_GFX1250_W4A8_FLYDSL_MIN_TOKENS` defaults to 384. In serving the MoE sees decode batches of at most the decode graph size (64 in the benchmarks below) and prefill buckets of 832-3072 tokens (1k prompts, 3072-token chunks); at most 5% of prefill steps fall between. So any value from 128 to 1024 serves about the same (predicted within 0.6% from the batch census and the per-layer times; measured at 256, 768 and 1024: throughput within the control drift, 768 and 1024 raised one point's median TTFT by ~4%). At 16, decode batches of 16-64 tokens run FlyDSL: -19% throughput (table below).
- The prepared weights are copied into a `torch.cuda.MemPool` of their own. Without it the caching allocator kept 13.6 GiB of reserved-but-free segments after the prep (each pinned by a piece of a padded buffer), which SGLang counted as weight memory and took from the KV pool. Outputs bitwise unchanged.
- Expert parallelism keeps the existing path. `SGLANG_GFX1250_W4A8_KERNEL_GATHER=1` together with the switch is refused (the Gluon path takes preshuffled weights).
- Unit test `test/registered/amd/test_gpt_oss_w4a8_flydsl_moe_gfx1250.py` (stage-b 1-GPU AMD, ~60 s; skips off gfx1250 or without AITER's FlyDSL grouped MoE): synthetic MXFP4 experts at gpt-oss's hidden size 2880 and the TP1/TP2 intermediate sizes, nonzero biases. Covers the dispatch boundary (MIN-1 Gluon, MIN and MIN+1 FlyDSL), Gluon views vs the Triton path (bitwise), FlyDSL vs an fp32 dequantized reference (rel. L2 < 0.03), finite outputs, unchanged weights, and the switch off (stock layout and output). It fails, as it should, with the Gluon views at the real K = 2880 and on an AITER without ROCm/aiter#6663.

## Accuracy Tests

`amd/gpt-oss-120b-w-mxfp4-a-fp8`, gfx1250 (MI450-series), images `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.22-rocm101-mi45x-20261027` and `-20261028`, AITER 2bb549102 + #6663 + the decode-store fix. GSM8K: 1319 questions, thinking, on a fresh server **after** fixed-seq 8192/1024 c16 + 1024/1024 c16 load (the protocol that exposed the race above).

- TP1, this PR at `MIN_TOKENS=384`: 0.9636 / 0.9621 / 0.9613 (three servers); with the MemPool commit 0.9613.
- With the AITER decode-store fix: 12 of 12 gate runs pass at TP2 and TP1; on the final stack TP1 0.9591 / 0.9613, TP2 0.9606.
- After each layout of a full benchmark suite, switch off -> this PR: TP1 0.9598 -> 0.9606, 2xTP1 0.9591 / 0.9538 -> 0.9591 / 0.9613, TP2 0.9621 -> 0.9583.

No truncated answers in any passing run. Layer check on real weights (TP1 layers 0/18/35, both TP2 ranks; 1-3072 tokens incl. 63/64/65 and 383/384/385; router and skewed routing): Gluon views vs the Triton path bitwise identical in all 130 rows; FlyDSL vs an fp32 reference rel. L2 0.02-0.07, the same distance as the Triton path; no NaN/Inf; weights unchanged after all calls.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

InferenceX fixed-seq, range ratio 0.8, run 1, output tok/s; TP1 on one gfx1250 partition.

**Threshold** (same box, fresh server per arm, A/B/A with 3-4 controls at 384; control drift <= 1.7%):

| ISL/OSL, conc | MIN 384 (control median) | MIN 16 | MIN 256 | MIN 768 | MIN 1024 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1024/1024 c4 | 841.3 | -0.6% | +0.3% | -0.1%* | -0.8% |
| 1024/1024 c64 | 4213.8 | **-19.1%** | +0.0% | -0.2%* | -0.6% |
| 8192/1024 c16 | 1328.8 | **-19.7%** | -0.1% | -0.1% | -0.3% |
| 8192/1024 c64 | 2062.8 | **-10.4%** | +0.1% | +0.0% | -0.0% |

\* repeat arm; the first MIN 768 run at 1k/1k c64 fell into a fast window (+8%) of the kind one control also hit.

FlyDSL for every batch (`MIN_TOKENS=1`) instead of 384, TP1 (A/B/A on a later stack): 0.60 / 0.69 (1k/1k c4 / c16), 0.65 / 0.76 (8k/1k c4 / c16).

## Known limitations

- **Memory.** The FlyDSL layout pads to 256: with the switch on the weights take 68.9 GB after loading instead of 61.2 GB (TP1; TP2 34.6 vs 30.7 GB per rank), so the TP1 KV pool is 987,776 tokens instead of 1,213,504. Padding to 128 needs AITER's FlyDSL MXFP8 activation quant to accept a feature dim that is not a multiple of 256 (it asserts today).
- **Gluon MoE decode race**: It was captured in TP2 GSM8K test. TP1 GSM8K almost always survive GSM8K full round.  The race can only be detected with finer-grained tests into LDS rows.  The root cause is complex.  [A known fix in LLVM upstream](https://lists.llvm.org/pipermail/llvm-commits/Week-of-Mon-20260803/2001738.html) mitigates this a lot but not cut to zero.  Still need further investigation.
- Off by default; `EP` keeps the existing path.

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

+"""gfx1250 GPT-OSS W4A8 MoE with SGLANG_GFX1250_W4A8_FLYDSL: FlyDSL a8w4 from
+SGLANG_GFX1250_W4A8_FLYDSL_MIN_TOKENS tokens up, gluon below it over zero-copy
+views of the same (FlyDSL-layout) weights.
+
+Synthetic MXFP4 experts with gpt-oss's hidden size 2880, which is not a
+multiple of 128: FlyDSL's weights are padded to 3072 and the gluon views cut at
+2944. The intermediate size is the TP1 one (2880) and the TP2 one (1440).
+Guards:
+- dispatch: MIN_TOKENS - 1 tokens run the gluon path, MIN_TOKENS and
+  MIN_TOKENS + 1 run FlyDSL;
+- the gluon views give exactly the stock Triton result. At K = 2880 the
+  GFX1250_SCALE scale descriptor ends at K // 32 groups while the layout keeps
+  K in 128-wide chunks, so views cut at the real dims read the last chunk's
+  scales as 0;
+- FlyDSL stays close to an fp32 dequantized reference with nonzero biases. An
+  AITER without ROCm/aiter#6663 adds the first N tile's bias to every N tile;
+- outputs are finite, and the calls leave the weights unchanged;
+- with the switch off, the weights and outputs are the stock path's.
+"""
+
+import functools
+import unittest
+from unittest import mock
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.layers.moe.moe_runner import MoeRunnerConfig
+from sglang.srt.layers.moe.token_dispatcher import StandardDispatchOutput
+from sglang.srt.layers.moe.topk import StandardTopKOutput
+from sglang.srt.utils.common import is_gfx1250_supported
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_amd_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_amd_ci(est_time=60, suite="stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd")
+
+_HIDDEN = 2880
+_NUM_EXPERTS = 8
+_TOP_K = 4
+_ALPHA = 1.702
+_LIMIT = 7.0
+_MIN_TOKENS = 384
+# Static per-tensor FP8 activation scales. The Triton path clips activations at
+# 448 * scale and FlyDSL (per-1x32 MXFP8) does not, so inputs beyond the range
+# would make two correct paths disagree: x stays within +-6 < 7, and the SwiGLU
+# output is bounded by limit * (limit + 1) = 56.
+_A13_SCALE = 7.0 / 448
+_A2_SCALE = 56.0 / 448
+# FlyDSL quantizes activations to MXFP8 (per-1x32 power-of-two scales) and
+# rounds GEMM 1's output to bf16 first: rel. L2 0.012-0.018 from the reference
+# here, the Triton path 0.003. Without ROCm/aiter#6663's bias fix: 0.55.
+_FLYDSL_REL_L2_TOL = 0.03
+
+_FP4_VALUES = (0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6, -0.0, -0.5, -1, -1.5, -2, -3, -4, -6)
+
+
+def _flydsl_available() -> bool:
+    if not is_gfx1250_supported():
+        return False
+    try:
+        import aiter.ops.flydsl.grouped_moe_gfx1250  # noqa: F401
+    except ImportError:
+        return False
+    return True
+
+
+def _dequant_mxfp4(w: torch.Tensor, scale: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """[..., N, K // 2] uint8 (low nibble first), [..., N, K // 32] e8m0 -> fp32."""
+    lut = torch.tensor(_FP4_VALUES, device=w.device)
+    v = torch.stack([lut[(w & 15).long()], lut[(w >> 4).long()]], dim=-1)
+    return v.flatten(-2) * torch.exp2(scale.float() - 127).repeat_interleave(32, -1)
+
+
+def _fp8(x: torch.Tensor, scale: float) -> torch.Tensor:
+    return (x / scale).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn).float() * scale
+
+
+def _reference(x, router_logits, w13, w13_scale, w13_bias, w2, w2_scale, w2_bias):
+    """gpt-oss MoE in fp32 over the loaded (gate/up separated) weights, with
+    both GEMMs' activations rounded to FP8 at the static scales."""
+    inter = w13.shape[1] // 2
+    vals, ids = torch.topk(router_logits.float(), _TOP_K, dim=-1)
+    weights = torch.softmax(vals, dim=-1)
+    out = torch.zeros(x.shape, dtype=torch.float32, device=x.device)
+    for e in ids.unique().tolist():
+        rows, slot = (ids == e).nonzero(as_tuple=True)
+        h = _fp8(x[rows].float(), _A13_SCALE) @ _dequant_mxfp4(w13[e], w13_scale[e]).T
+        h = h + w13_bias[e]
+        gate = h[:, :inter].clamp(max=_LIMIT)
+        up = h[:, inter:].clamp(-_LIMIT, _LIMIT)
+        act = _fp8(gate * torch.sigmoid(_ALPHA * gate) * (up + 1), _A2_SCALE)
+        y = act @ _dequant_mxfp4(w2[e], w2_scale[e]).T + w2_bias[e]
+        out.index_add_(0, rows, y * weights[rows, slot, None])
+    return out
+
+
+def _rel_l2(a: torch.Tensor, b: torch.Tensor) -> float:
+    return ((a.float() - b.float()).norm() / b.float().norm()).item()
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(_flydsl_available(), "requires an AMD gfx1250 GPU with FlyDSL")
+class TestGptOssW4A8FlydslMoEGfx1250(CustomTestCase):
+    @classmethod
+    def setUpClass(cls):
+        from sglang.srt.layers.moe.fused_moe_triton import aiter_mxfp4_w4a8_moe
+        from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.quark.schemes import (
+            quark_w4a8_mxfp4_moe,
+        )
+
+        cls.moe = aiter_mxfp4_w4a8_moe
+        cls.scheme_module = quark_w4a8_mxfp4_moe
+        cls.gen = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(0)
+
+    def _random_loaded_weights(self, inter: int):
+        """What the Quark loader leaves in the layer: gate/up separated."""
+
+        def fp4(*shape):
+            return torch.randint(
+                0, 256, shape, generator=self.gen, device="cuda", dtype=torch.uint8
+            )
+
+        def e8m0(*shape):
+            # 2^-7 .. 2^-5: gate/up pre-activations of a few units.
+            return torch.randint(
+                120, 123, shape, generator=self.gen, device="cuda", dtype=torch.uint8
+            )
+
+        def randn(*shape):
+            return torch.randn(shape, generator=self.gen, device="cuda")
+
+        return dict(
+            w13_weight=fp4(_NUM_EXPERTS, 2 * inter, _HIDDEN // 2),
+            w13_weight_scale=e8m0(_NUM_EXPERTS, 2 * inter, _HIDDEN // 32),
+            w13_weight_bias=randn(_NUM_EXPERTS, 2 * inter),
+            w2_weight=fp4(_NUM_EXPERTS, _HIDDEN, inter // 2),
+            w2_weight_scale=e8m0(_NUM_EXPERTS, _HIDDEN, inter // 32),
+            w2_weight_bias=2 * randn(_NUM_EXPERTS, _HIDDEN),
+        )
+
+    def _make_layer(self, loaded: dict, flydsl: bool):
+        scheme = self.scheme_module.QuarkW4A8MXFp4MoE(
+            weight_config=dict(
+                dtype="fp4",
+                qscheme="per_group",
+                group_size=32,
+                is_dynamic=False,
+                scale_format="e8m0",
+            ),
+            input_config=dict(dtype="fp8_e4m3", qscheme="per_tensor", is_dynamic=False),
+        )
+        layer = torch.nn.Module()
+        inter = loaded["w2_weight"].shape[-1] * 2
+        with torch.device("cuda"):
+            scheme.create_weights(
+                layer,
+                num_experts=_NUM_EXPERTS,
+                hidden_size=_HIDDEN,
+                intermediate_size_per_partition=inter,
+                params_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+                with_bias=True,
+            )
+        for name, value in loaded.items():
+            getattr(layer, name).data.copy_(value)
+        layer.w13_input_scale.data.fill_(_A13_SCALE)
+        layer.w2_input_scale.data.fill_(_A2_SCALE)
+        with mock.patch.object(self.moe, "FLYDSL_ENABLED", flydsl):
+            scheme.process_weights_after_loading(layer)
+        scheme.create_moe_runner(
+            layer,
+            MoeRunnerConfig(
+                activation="swiglu", gemm1_alpha=_ALPHA, gemm1_clamp_limit=_LIMIT
+            ),
+        )
+        return scheme, layer
+
+    def _inputs(self, num_tokens: int):
+        x = torch.randn(num_tokens, _HIDDEN, generator=self.gen, device="cuda")
+        x = x.clamp(-6, 6).bfloat16()
+        # Distinct logits: bf16 ties at the 4th/5th expert would let the Triton
+        # routing and torch.topk pick different, equally valid experts.
+        logits = torch.stack(
+            [
+                torch.randperm(_NUM_EXPERTS, generator=self.gen, device="cuda")
+                for _ in range(num_tokens)
+            ]
+        )
+        return x, (logits * 0.5).bfloat16()
+
+    def _apply(self, scheme, layer, x, router_logits):
+        topk_weights, topk_ids = torch.topk(router_logits.float(), _TOP_K, dim=-1)
+        dispatch_output = StandardDispatchOutput(
+            hidden_states=x,
+            hidden_states_scale=None,
+            topk_output=StandardTopKOutput(
+                topk_weights.softmax(dim=-1), topk_ids.int(), router_logits
+            ),
+        )
+        with mock.patch.object(self.moe, "FLYDSL_MIN_TOKENS", _MIN_TOKENS):
+            return scheme.apply_weights(layer, dispatch_output).hidden_states
+
+    def _triton(self, stock, x, router_logits):
+        """The stock path's layout on the Triton backend."""
+        return self.moe.aiter_w4a8_gfx1250_forward(
+            hidden_states=x,
+            router_logits=router_logits,
+            topk=_TOP_K,
+            a13_scale=torch.tensor(_A13_SCALE, device="cuda"),
+            a2_scale=torch.tensor(_A2_SCALE, device="cuda"),
+            gemm1_alpha=_ALPHA,
+            gemm1_limit=_LIMIT,
+            backend="triton",
+            **stock,
+        )
+
+    def _check_switch(self, inter: int):
+        loaded = self._random_loaded_weights(inter)
+        stock = dict(
+            zip(
+                loaded.keys(),
+                self.moe.prepare_w4a8_gfx1250_weights(
+                    *[t.clone() for t in loaded.values()]
+                ),
+            )
+        )
+        scheme, layer = self._make_layer(loaded, flydsl=True)
+        fw = scheme.flydsl_weights
+        self.assertIsNotNone(fw)
+        # One weight copy: the parameters are FlyDSL's buffers.
+        self.assertEqual(layer.w13_weight.data_ptr(), fw.w13.data_ptr())
+        self.assertEqual(layer.w2_weight.data_ptr(), fw.w2.data_ptr())
+        params = {n: p.detach().clone() for n, p in layer.named_parameters()}
+
+        for num_tokens in (1, _MIN_TOKENS - 1, _MIN_TOKENS, _MIN_TOKENS + 1, 1024):
+            with self.subTest(inter=inter, num_tokens=num_tokens):
+                x, router_logits = self._inputs(num_tokens)
+                out = self._apply(scheme, layer, x, router_logits)
+                self.assertEqual(tuple(out.shape), (num_tokens, _HIDDEN))
+                self.assertTrue(torch.isfinite(out).all())
+                triton = self._triton(stock, x, router_logits)
+                if num_tokens < _MIN_TOKENS:
+                    # Gluon over FlyDSL's weights: the Triton result, bit for bit.
+                    self.assertTrue(
+                        torch.equal(out, triton),
+                        f"gluon vs triton max abs diff "
+                        f"{(out.float() - triton.float()).abs().max().item()}",
+                    )
+                else:
+                    # FlyDSL: not the gluon/Triton result, but within tolerance
+                    # of the fp32 reference.
+                    self.assertFalse(torch.equal(out, triton))
+                    ref = _reference(x, router_logits, *loaded.values())
+                    rel = _rel_l2(out, ref)
+                    self.assertLess(rel, _FLYDSL_REL_L2_TOL, f"FlyDSL rel L2 {rel}")
+
+        for name, p in layer.named_parameters():
+            self.assertTrue(torch.equal(p, params[name]), f"{name} changed")
+
+    def test_switch_tp1_intermediate(self):
+        self._check_switch(inter=2880)
+
+    def test_switch_tp2_intermediate(self):
+        self._check_switch(inter=1440)
+
+    def test_switch_off_keeps_the_stock_path(self):
+        loaded = self._random_loaded_weights(1440)
+        stock = dict(
+            zip(
+                loaded.keys(),
+                self.moe.prepare_w4a8_gfx1250_weights(
+                    *[t.clone() for t in loaded.values()]
+                ),
+            )
+        )
+        scheme, layer = self._make_layer(loaded, flydsl=False)
+        self.assertIsNone(scheme.flydsl_weights)
+        for name, expected in stock.items():
+            p = getattr(layer, name)
+            self.assertEqual(p.shape, expected.shape, name)
+            self.assertEqual(p.stride(), expected.stride(), name)
+            self.assertTrue(torch.equal(p, expected), name)
+        # Pin the stock path's backend to Triton, as the gfx1250 recipes do: its
+        # default (gluon over the unshuffled layout) is not reproducible run to
+        # run from a few hundred tokens on this AITER.
+        triton_forward = functools.partial(
+            self.moe.aiter_w4a8_gfx1250_forward, backend="triton"
+        )
+        for num_tokens in (1, _MIN_TOKENS, 1024):
+            with self.subTest(num_tokens=num_tokens):
+                x, router_logits = self._inputs(num_tokens)
+                with mock.patch.object(
+                    self.moe, "aiter_w4a8_gfx1250_forward", triton_forward
+                ):
+                    out = self._apply(scheme, layer, x, router_logits)
+                self.assertTrue(torch.equal(out, self._triton(stock, x, router_logits)))
+

+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
